articleTitle: Grid-Connected Inverter DC Voltage Self-Immunity Control Strategy Based on 5G+Photovoltaic Power Prediction Feedforward
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: To mitigate the issues of voltage instability and slow response speed in grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems caused by PV output fluctuations and delays or packet losses in network transmission, an improved active disturbance rejection control strategy is proposed. Specifically, a two-stage PV grid-connected power generation system topology is established, and the traditional control method of the voltage outer loop and current inner loop is thoroughly analyzed. On this basis, a 5G+ PV power prediction feedforward segment is added. By combining adaptive functions with the Variable Gain Sliding Mode Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (VGSM-LADRC) strategy, adaptive adjustment of voltage control is achieved. Simulation results show that compared to traditional control strategies, the proposed strategy reduces the peak value of DC voltage fluctuations by 0.73V and decreases the DC voltage overshoot by 27.5%.

articleTitle: On Efficient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Large Scale Supply Demand Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The current technology advances in renewable power generation, fuel cell, and storage devices push forward the growing research interest on supply demand matching in smart grid, which could involve hundreds of thousands of agents making decisions in real time. In this multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problem, the key questions are what to share and how to utilize the shared information. These questions remain open due to the complexity and difference among the subproblems of each agent. We consider this important problem in this work, and make the following major contributions. First, we formulate the problem to maximize the probability of correctly selecting (PCS) the best action for each agent under limited sampling budget. Second, we clarify what to be shared among the agents and quantify the value of such shared information. Third, we present an algorithm to asymptotically maximize the PCS. We hope this work shed light on MARL in general.

articleTitle: LSTM Parameter Optimization Based on Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm and NSGAII
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is a commonly used model for time series data. However, its model performance and generalization ability heavily depend on the parameter configuration. Therefore, it is necessary to study parameter optimization for the LSTM model. Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) holds advantages over the traditional optimization algorithms in several aspects. However, it still faces some challenges. Therefore, based on SSA, this paper introduces three strategies to improve it: Levy flight strategy, sine search strategy, and step size factor adjustment strategy. The resulting algorithm is called the Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA). Then, we establish the ISSA-LSTM model. Additionally, to address the limitations of SSA in dealing with multi-objective problems, we introduce the Fast Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGAII) and establish the ISSA-NSGAII model. Finally, the experimental validation demonstrates the superiority of the proposed algorithm in optimizing parameters for the LSTM model.

articleTitle: Improved TCN-Vine Copula Method for Wind Speed Prediction Using 5G+ Technology Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Accurate wind speed prediction can facilitate the efficient utilization of wind energy. Therefore, a prediction method combining improved temporal convolutional network (TCN) with vine copula using 5G+ technology data transmission is proposed. Initially, the residual module in TCN is improved by using the attention mechanism and soft thresholding concept from deep residual shrinkage network (DRSN) for preliminary prediction. Subsequently, given the influence of meteorological factors on wind speed, the meteorological data are downscaled by using the kernel principal component analysis (KPCA), which reduces the complexity of the data under the premise of guaranteeing the complete features. Finally, a correction model based on vine copula is constructed, and the preliminary prediction values is corrected using the downscaled meteorological data to obtain the final prediction results. This paper takes wind turbines in a wind farm as the experimental subjects, and utilizes sensors and 5G+ technology to collect wind speed and related meteorological data. Experiments using measured data verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Vision Transformers Based on Prompt Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Currently, in the field of deep learning, the “pre-train and fine-tune” paradigm has become the mainstream training method for many network models due to the increased capacity of network models and the variety of tasks. However, fine-tuning has become increasingly challenging, as a new model needs to be fine-tuned for each task, which consumes a lot of time and computational resources. This paper proposes an unsupervised domain-adapted image classification method based on prompt learning and Vision Transformer. Unlike the traditional “pre-training, fine-tuning” paradigm, the method applies the pre-trained models of prompt learning and Vision Transformer to the unsupervised domain adaptation task, and proposes to redefine image classification as a mask prediction task. Specifically, the pre-trained model is guided by constructing templates and labeled word sets for prompt learning. Then, the image classification problem is converted into the form of a complete blank and embedded into the constructed template, and the labeled words corresponding to the maximum probability are selected and mapped back to the set of labeled words by the pre-trained model. By conducting experiments on several UDA benchmark datasets, including 93.5% for Office-31, 83.30% for Office-Home, and 81.97% for VisDA-2017, it can be demonstrated that prompt learning greatly improves the efficiency of using the pre-trained model and saves computational resources without significantly affecting the model performance.

articleTitle: Mixup Enhanced Linear Robust Explainable Model for Identifying Key Factors of Surface Defects in Strip Steel Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The surface defect is a common defect in strip steel products, which can seriously affect the various properties of the strip steel. This paper aims to propose a key influencing factor identification indicators based on the idea of explainable artificial intelligent to assist engineers in locating key variables related to surface defects. In the practical application, the obtained data show the characteristic of imbalance, and the defect data severely overlaps with the normal data, which makes it difficult to fully extract defect-related information. To address these challenges, in this paper, a novel fine-gained defect label is designed for constructing the supervised defect-related model, meanwhile, a Mixup based strategy is established to improve the robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Wearable Dual-Channel Transcutaneous Acupoint Electrical Stimulator Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In recent years, as an effective means to relieve pain instead of traditional acupuncture, transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulation has attracted much attention. In this paper, a wearable two-channel transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulator based on STM32 is designed. The device can adjust the stimulation parameters in real time through the mobile phone APP, including the selection of stimulation channels, frequency and amplitude adjustment. The results show that the pulse width of the stimulus is 1ms, which can be adjusted in real time at the frequency of 2-100Hz and the amplitude of 0-30mA. The bipolar pulse output is supported, and the high and low frequency waveform interleaving constant current output can be achieved to ensure the stability and effectiveness of the stimulus. The wearable double-channel transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulator designed in this paper has the advantages of high portability and intelligence, and has certain clinical and commercial value.

Author Keywords: transcutaneous electrical stimulation of acupuncture points

articleTitle: Robust UDE-Based Saturated Control for Quadrotors in Waypoint Tracking Flights
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the waypoint tracking problem of a quadrotor in the presence of external interference and actuator saturation. Specifically, the saturation issue induced by the waypoint switching in classic feedback control is systematically addressed. The dynamic model of quadrotor is first provided and then simplified into six second-order subsystems. Based on this model, a UDE-based saturated control is proposed to achieve position tracking while avoiding actuator saturation in waypoint flights, thus improving the transient performance of the system. The stability of the proposed control system is proved using the algebraic theory for linear time-varying systems. Comparative simulation results show performance advantage of the proposed control over the classic cascade PID controller and bounded UDE-based controller.

articleTitle: Conservative Q-Learning Based Furnace Temperature Control in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The nonlinear, time-varying, and lagging nature of the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process presents challenges for ensuring controller safety. While offline reinforcement learning (RL) can ensure safety in furnace temperature (FT) control, its performance is hindered by extrapolation errors, making it unsuitable for direct application in the incineration environment. To address this, we propose a conservative Q-learning-based furnace temperature control strategy (CQL-FTC). This strategy involves two stages: online sampling and offline training. During the online sampling stage, the agent interacts with the environment to collect samples, building an experience replay buffer (ERB) and performing pretraining. In the offline training stage, we introduce the CQL method, adding constraint terms to the traditional Bellman equation to minimize extrapolation errors. After offline training, the agent is directly applied to the FT setpoint control in the incineration process. Simulation results using the actual MSWI process dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in complex industrial environments.

articleTitle: Robotic Arm Target Grasping Algorithm Based on Obstacle Removal in Space-Constrained Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Achieving precise grasping of specific targets in complex and crowded scenes is of great importance. Existing works often rely on the combination of pushing and grasping strategies to separate the target from surrounding obstacles. However, in crowded environments with limited space, traditional combined push-grasp methods struggle to effectively separate the target from dense obstacles due to insufficient action execution space. To address the problem of target grasping in space-constrained scenes, this paper proposes a target grasping algorithm based on policy search mechanism. By intelligently identifying and grasping the obstacles around the target, the complexity of the workspace is reduced, thereby improving the action efficiency and the success rate of target grasping. Firstly, a Q-value prediction network is trained based on deep reinforcement learning to extract features from input images and predict the Q-value of each pixel point to determine the best grasping point. Secondly, to improve the network's prediction ability, the SE-DenseNet network structure is proposed for feature extraction and enhancing the network's sensitivity to key feature information. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed grasping framework, a space-constrained working scene is built in the CoppeliaSim simulation platform for experimental testing. The results show that the proposed framework achieves an action efficiency of 82.6% and a grasping success rate of 83.5%, significantly outperforming traditional methods. Moreover, the impact of each part of the algorithm on system performance is further verified through ablation studies, fully demonstrating the efficiency and reliability of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Classification of Steel Strip Surface Defects Based on Depthwise-Separable Convolution and Cross-Scale Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In the production process of steel strips, it is important to distinguish and classify its surface defects. In this paper, the ResNet-50 model is improved to enhance its performance on the task of steel strip defect classification. Aiming at the problem of small samples of industrial defect datasets, six data augmentation methods are applied to expand the original dataset and improve the robustness of the model. Usually, steel strip defects account for a small percentage of the whole image, so it is proposed to add the Efficient Multi-scale Attention module (EMA) after each residual block of ResNet-50 to make the model more focused on the defective regions. At the same time, the computational efficiency of the model is improved by replacing the ordinary convolution of the model with Depthwise-Separable convolution. Finally, the model is trained and tested with the proposed improved ResN et-50 model on a dataset containing six types of steel strip surface defects. The experimental results show that the proposed model can classify defects with an accuracy of 99.1%.

articleTitle: Cloud Manufacturing Dynamic Composition Reconfiguration Method Under Resource Exception
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The initial production plan formulated by the cloud platform in actual production is prone to various uncertain interference such as equipment failure and order cancellation, resulting in the realization of the established production plan. Therefore, this paper proposes a dynamic reconfiguration method for cloud manufacturing resources under abnormal condition. First, the fundamental manufacturing scheme is generated ac-cording to the initial functional optimization objectives. Then, for the uncertain interference factors in the cloud manufacturing environment, three optimization strategies are used to dynami-cally reconstruct the manufacturing scheme of the interference points based on the principle of minimum change, and an improved differential evolution algorithm is used to optimize the reconstruction scheme. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Interpretation of ADRC in $Q$-Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper presents a control structure featuring an operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> driven by the residual signal, which indicates the difference between the measurement output and the estimated output from an observer. The form of this observer is very general, as long as it can generate the estimated state or relevant information that will be incorporated into this control structure. The operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> introduces an extra design freedom to address uncertainties, such that linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) can be interpreted as a special case in the Q-structure when a linear extended state observer is used.

articleTitle: Learning and Operator Based Control System Design for Soft Robotic Finger with Denial of Service Attack and Input Hysteresis Using Right Coprime Factorization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Network attacks generally occurred in practical control system and possibly cause instability even insecurity. Specifically, Denial of Service (DoS) attack is the one that could cut down the connection between equipment and make the feedback signal zero consequently. In this paper, a machine learning based control system design is proposed to deal with the problems caused by DoS attack and input hysteresis in the case of soft robotic finger. The system is accomplished using right coprime factorization (RCF) theory, by which the robust stability of proposed system is guaranteed. In addition, the results of practical experiments are exhibited as well to verify the effectiveness of proposed system.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Blade Positioning and Defect Recognition via SCNs and YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The maintenance of blades is essential for the stable and safe operation of wind turbines to ensure power generation efficiency. However, the low positioning efficiency of wind turbine blades and the difficulty in feature extraction of blade surface defects make the detection and recognition of wind turbine blade defects challenging. Therefore, combined with artificial intelligence transfer learning, YOLOv5 is proposed to extract the blade area in a complex background, and then the fine-tuned ResNet18 is used to extract the feature of the blade area to obtain the feature vector with a length of 512. Finally, Stochastic Configuration Networks (SCNs) is used to classify the data obtained by dimensionality reduction. The experimental results show that the AP: 50 of YOLOv5 reaches 99.5%, and the defect classification accuracy of SCNs reaches 97.2%. This method can accurately and quickly locate the position of wind turbine blades and identify the type of blade defects.

articleTitle: Variable Neighborhood Search for Scheduling of Cold Rolling Annealing Process of Silicon Steel*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Aiming at the production scheduling problem of cold rolling annealing process of silicon steel, a multi-objective optimization model of production scheduling is established, which considered various process constraints such as steel grade switch, width jump, annealing temperature jump, etc. The multi-objective functions are transformed into a single objective function by weighted sum method. Based on the characteristics of the problem, four kinds of neighborhood structures for local search are proposed. And a variable neighborhood search algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. The correctness of the model and the effectiveness of the algorithm are verified by practical production instances. The experimental results show that the approximate Pareto solution set with good distribution can be obtained by using the weighted sum method and solved by the variable neighborhood search algorithm proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Can We Characterize Variabilities of Variabilities in Real Time?
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Variabilities are inherent in complex natural and man-made systems including complex big data in industrial processes. Characterization of variabilities becomes a foundation of industrial AI(IAI). Traditional methods to measure variability such as variance, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z$</tex>-score etc. do not work for complex data series such as random processes with heavy-tailedness in distribution or long-range dependence (LRD). Both types are of fractal nature with a self-similarity (SS) property that follows an inverse power law (IPL) trend. The Hurst parameter is a dimensionless factor used to characterize the presence and magnitude of the self-similarity property. Many existing Hurst parameter estimators are for offline or batch processing, when, in real applications, stream processing or online real-time processing is needed. A moving window method is used for online estimation of Hurst parameters in our previous paper with a detailed investigation on which estimator performs best for online processing, the effects of window sizes, and computational cost evaluation. In this work, we extend the previous study to time-varying Hurst parameters where the Hurst parameter may have its own variability. The key contributions in this paper are 1) two signal generators in Matlab that generate a random process with given desirable Hurst curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(t) with numerical verification; 2) moving window Aggregate Variance method implemented in Simulink for stream processing to estimate Ĥ (t) with various <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(t) shapes such as ramp, square, sawtooth and sine waves. To demonstrate the variabilities of variabilities characterization ability of this work, a special example is given for a case when H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(t) itself is a fractional Gaussian noise (fGn) with a constant Hurst parameter H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> where we can use the estimated constant Ĥ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in the obtained Ĥ(t). It is interesting to see that the possibility of characterizing the variabilities in variability is enabled using the tools presented in this work.

articleTitle: Gradient-Free High-Order Accelerated Self Optimizing Control of Processes with Time Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: A self-optimizing controller (SOC) adds an upper optimization layer to closed-loop systems, enhancing self-awareness and improving performance during repetitive tasks. However, most SOC optimization algorithms use only the current and previous cost function evaluations to determine the next optimal parameters (first-order optimization methods). This paper introduces a high-order self-optimizing controller (HOSOC) that accelerates the optimization algorithm's convergence by utilizing the history of optimal parameters within a sliding window. A modified version of the Globalized Constrained Nelder Mead optimization method is implemented to account for the past centroids within a memory window to compute the upcoming solution. The algorithm is tested on a general delay-aware First-Order plus Dead Time (FOPDT) system with varying lag, balanced, and delay time dynamics. Results show that the high-order SOC controller speeds up convergence and meets the desired performance specifications effectively.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Adaptive Event-Triggered Control for Stochastic Nonlinear Systems with Output Constraint and Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of finite-time event-triggered command filtered adaptive neural network tracking control for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems (SNS) with output constraint and input saturation. The adaptive neural networks are utilized to approximate the unknown nonlinear terms, while the barrier Lyapunov function is employed to confine the system output signal within a predefined range. By integrating the event trigger (ET) mechanism with finite-time (FT) command filtered technique, the system's finite-time stability can be ensured, while also reducing communication costs. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Global Prescribed Performance Control of MIMO Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the tracking con-trol problem with prescribed performance for multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) nonlinear systems. The prescribed performance means that the system outputs track the given trajectories with the arbitrarily predefined speed of response and accuracy. Most prescribed performance control (PPC) solutions for MIMO systems fail to achieve global tracking performance. Therefore, global performance envelops are constructed to con-fine the tracking errors, and the barrier functions are used to combat these errors. Consequently, a robust PPC scheme is developed. In this way, the predefined performance is achieved for any initial condition. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Prediction of Powder Delivery Amount With Polyethylene Belt-Loaded Powder
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Electroexplosive powdering, as an emerging method of ultrafine powder preparation, has the powder feeding amount as a key factor affecting the quality of explosive products. To achieve stable and accurate micro powder feeding, an X-axis linear motor-driven polyethylene belt-loaded powder molding device was constructed and powder feeding experiments were conducted. By analyzing the factors affecting the powder feeding amount, a mixed prediction model for the powder feeding amount was established. Experimental verification showed that the prediction results meet the practical requirements of the powder electroexplosion method, providing a solution for the accurate prediction and control of the powder feeding amount.

articleTitle: Plume Finding with Frontier-Based Planner
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Toxic/hazardous gas leaks seriously jeopardize public safety and the ecological environment, and how to utilize drones with on-board gas sensors to quickly detect gas plumes at an early stage of a gas leak and take timely measures can effectively prevent the expansion of the accident. Traditional plume finding methods have the disadvantages of poor targeting, long search times, and repeated exploration in some areas. In view of this, this paper proposes a method of plume finding with frontier-based planner, where a heuristic function is designed to select optimal observation points and thus plan path to search plume. Here an air-mass path model is constructed to estimate the region that would likely be observed by the UAV at a candidate observation site on the frontier, and the area of the unknown part in the region is considered as the environmental exploration gain. The change in flight direction and the distance traveled by the UAV are used as environmental exploration costs when it will fly from its current pose to the candidate observation site. Simulation results show that the proposed frontier-based exploration method for plume finding has good performance in odor source localization tasks in outdoor environments.

articleTitle: Camera-Based Dynamic Vibration Measurement Using CoTracker Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the CoTracker model, a sophisticated deep learning approach based on transformer architecture, for its application in dynamic vibration measurement using vision cameras. Compared to traditional accelerometers, which are costly and limited to point-based measurements, CoTracker promises a cost-effective, full-field analysis by tracking pixel movements in video sequences. We applied this model to analyze the vibrations of a cantilever beam captured through a high-speed camera, comparing its output against data from a standard reference accelerometer. Our findings suggest that CoTracker could revolutionize structural vibration monitoring due to its efficiency and broad applicability.

articleTitle: Rapid Simulation Method for Electro-Pneumatic Composite Braking System Based on Equivalent Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Ahstract-The electro-pneumatic braking system (EPBS), abbreviated as the braking system, serves as a crucial safety measure for the smooth operation of high-speed trains. Currently, research on the characteristics of electro-pneumatic braking heavily relies on AMESim co-simulation. However, this approach suffers from slow simulation speed due to increased model complexity, data exchange, and communication delays, significantly hindering the development of online simulation for braking system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a rapid simulation method for EPBS based on equivalent models, which substantially reduces simulation time while ensuring accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of 97.91% for the equivalent EP valve model, 99.32% for the equivalent empty-load valve model, 98.99% for the equivalent relay valve model, and 98.99% for the equivalent brake cylinder model. Furthermore, the equivalent EPBS simulation exhibits a speed enhancement of 16.98 times compared to co-simulation, thereby offering a new approach to accelerating the simulation of braking system.

articleTitle: Study of the Dynamics of Manipulated Droplet Based on Concave Spherical Phased Array Acoustic Levitator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Ultrasonic levitation is a unique technology that utilizes the nonlinear effect of ultrasonic wave to generate acoustic radiation force to achieve object levitation. This technology is suitable for containerless manipulation of liquid samples because it avoids contact with manipulated objects and is widely used in the fields of material preparation and biochemical analysis. In this paper, the dynamic behavior of a droplet in acoustic levitation and the velocity and position distribution of the droplet in the acoustic field under the acoustic radiation force were studied by using the finite element method. The droplet dynamic behavior was observed by using a concave spherical phased array acoustic levitator, and the droplet deformation, cavitation and oscillation under acoustic manipulation were studied. The results show that the droplet velocity and morphology can be controlled, and the droplet shaping can be achieved under the control of the concave spherical phased array acoustic levitator.

articleTitle: Application of GA-PSO-LSTM Model in Membrane Fouling Prediction in Wastewater Treatment Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Membrane bioreactor (MBR), as a new wastewater treatment and water recycling technology, is widely used in the field of water treatment. However, membrane contamination is an unavoidable problem in MBR operation, which seriously affects its utilization. Membrane permeability is an important indicator of membrane contamination, and the researcher proposed a membrane permeability prediction model based on long short-term memory neural network (LSTM). Firstly, the researcher used principal component analysis (PCA) to determine the process variables related to membrane permeability based on the actual operation data. Then, the membrane permeability prediction model was established based on the LSTM neural network, which has many parameters that need to be set, and the researcher used genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize these parameters, and the GA-LSTM model was trained and tested. The results showed that the model was able to predict the membrane water permeability with an RMSE of 0.78958. However, the convergence speed of the model was slow. However, the convergence speed of the model is slow. For this reason, the researcher introduced the particle swarm algorithm (PSO), and designed a hybrid algorithm of GA and PSO to optimize the initial parameters of LSTM, and established the GA-PSO-LSTM model for predicting the membrane water permeability. The results show that GA-PSO-LSTM has higher prediction accuracy than GA-LSTM, the RMSE of the model is only 0.21007, and the convergence speed is faster. GA-PSO-LSTM can accurately predict the membrane contamination, so that the maintenance personnel can carry out the maintenance and cleaning in time to prolong the life of the membrane, and to improve the effect of the application of membrane technology.

articleTitle: C02 Emission Concentration Modeling Method Based on LSTM in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The C02 emissions from municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) processes significantly influence dual-carbon goals and ecological environmental protection. This article proposes a method for modeling C02 emission concentrations based on long short-term memory (LSTM). Initially, the Z-Score method is applied to handle outliers. Subsequently, the mutual information (MI) algorithm assesses the correlation between features and C02 emissions, facilitating feature selection. Finally, the LSTM algorithm constructs a predictive model for C02 emission concentrations. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using real C02 data from the MSWI process in Beijing.

articleTitle: Effect of Voltage Waveform on the Drop Formation Dynamics in A Drop-on-Demand Inkjet Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Piezoelectric drop-on-demand inkjet technology is widely used in the field of additive manufacturing due to its advantages of cost-effective., high-precision., and efficient printing of multiple materials. However., there is a certain conflict between printing efficiency and printing quality in practical applications. So it is especially important to study the relationship between voltage waveform and droplet volume and velocity. In order to realize the precise control of droplet volume and velocity within the controllable range by adjusting the voltage waveform in the actual industrial production process. This paper establishes a coupled dynamics model of piezoelectric inkjet printhead., carries out a simulation study on the dynamics of the droplet injection process., and analyzes its formation mechanism. Based on the mechanism of droplet formation and the response characteristics of the basic waveform., experiments on droplet formation are carried out to study the effect of voltage waveform on the droplet formation process and droplet jetting quality. The experimental results show that the volume and velocity of droplets show an approximately linear growth trend with the increase of voltage amplitude. These works provide theoretical support for subsequent research and applications.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Estimation Based on Dynamic Event-triggered Mechanism and Interval Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fault estimation(FE) for a class of systems with dynamic event-triggered mecha-nism(ETM) in network environment is studied. In order to increase the interval between events and reduce the amount of data transmission, this paper introduces internal dynamic vari-ables into the event-triggered mechanism and modifies the event- triggered threshold. Then, for the augmented system composed of state vector and sensor fault vector, an interval observer is designed to ensure the interval property between the system state and its estimations, and to realize the simultaneous estimation of the system state and sensor fault. Moreover, the Metzler matrix is constructed by a same eigenvalue transformation(SET), and the FE problem of the reconstructed augmented model is redesigned. Finally, the main results are verified by numerical simulation, and the validity of the conclusions is verified.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Breast Cancer Ultrasound Medical Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data model for the recognition of medical images in breast cancer ultrasound examinations, based on convolutional neural networks (CNN). To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, experiments were conducted on 765 data samples, and four evaluation metrics-accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score-were calculated to analyse the classification performance of the trained model. The results indicate that the new CNN model achieves a minimum recognition accuracy of no less than 70% on the test set, demonstrating robust recognition performance and meeting the designed objectives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Soil Carbon Content Classification Using Transfer Learning and FrFT on Millimeter Wave Radar Array Signals with Varied Backgrounds
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The precise quantification of soil carbon content is crucial for understanding soil health and its impact on climate change. This study investigates the classification of soil carbon content using millimeter wave radar array signals, focusing on a comparative analysis of Support Vector Machines (SVM), Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), and Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) methods. Furthermore, raw time and CWT-processed signals using SVM are used as baseline to establish the fundamental classification performance. The key contribution of this research is the innovative use of FrFT, where the transformed signals are converted into images and subsequently fed into GoogLeNet through transfer learning. This approach leverages the powerful feature extraction capabilities of GoogleNet to enhance classification accuracy. Experiments were conducted on a dataset comprising millimeter wave signals reflecting varied backgrounds with the primary focus on one specific distance measurement. Results provided show that high resolution millimeter wave signals achieved up to 100% validation accuracy at multiple fractional orders. The improved accuracy highlights the potential of integrating advanced signal transformation methods with deep learning models for soil carbon content classification.

articleTitle: ViT-Based Hybrid Segmentation for Leftover Food Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In an aging society, the number of caregivers in the nursing care industry is decreasing and the number of persons requiring nursing care is increasing, resulting in a serious labor shortage. In addition, measurement of the amount of food intake by caregivers is an important element of caregiving work, however, the measurement standard is not standardized and is inaccurate because it is done by caregivers' visual measurement. This research utilizes deep learning-based image recognition AI to automate the measurement of food intake. Specifically, a new framework that simultaneously performs the separate tasks of segmentation and object detection using ViT is proposed to perform segmentation of leftover food and detection of eating utensils. Furthermore, based on these recognition results, an algorithm to estimate the volume of the leftover food is proposed and its accuracy is evaluated. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed Hybrid Segmentation method with ViT/8-small@224 at 89.25% mIoU in segmentation and 100.00% mAP, 95.47% mIoU for object detection. Future work includes updating the dataset and the leftover volume estimation method.

articleTitle: IGDT Robustness Analysis of Integrated Energy System with Uncertain Wind Power Access
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The access of uncertain wind power brings great challenges to the safe and economic operation of integrated energy system, so it is particularly important to analyze its robustness. However, due to the strong randomness and uncontrollability of wind power, the lack of the prerequisites for conventional robust analysis methods makes the robust analysis of integrated energy systems difficult. In this paper, the robustness of the system in four different scenarios, such as energy storage (ES) unit and combined heating and power (CHP), is analyzed by using the information gap decision theory. Simulation experiments show that the presence of ES units and CHP units in the system greatly enhances the ability to absorb uncertain wind power and effectively improve the robustness of the system.

articleTitle: A Triangular Six-Line Oversampling Method for Unbalanced Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: An improved triangle oversampling technique is introduced to address the challenge of data imbalance in industrial classification tasks. In this method, the new sample is synthesized precisely along the median line of the triangle, ensuring that it aligns with the mathematical expectation of the triangle's center. Furthermore, the variance of this newly synthesized sample, under the action of the regulator, closely approximates the variance of the original sample, effectively simulating the density distribution of raw data. The samples produced by this method exhibit a distribution similar to the original samples, and the efficacy of this proposed method has been validated through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Frequency-Mixing Nonlinear Detection of Microcracks in Metal Plates
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Detection of early microcracks in metallic structures is critical for analyzing structural failure and life prediction, Conventional Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) methods are not sensitive to the identification of microcracks in structures. In this paper, nonlinear ultrasonic mixing detection method is utilized for the study of microcrack damage detection. Based on the nonlinear wave theory, an ultrasonic nonlinear mixing model containing microcracks is established. The nonlinear interaction between two rows of single-frequency lamb waves in the same direction and collinear with the microcrack interface after mixing was analyzed, and the influence of the change of microcrack depth and width on the mixing modulation effect was studied. At the same time, the influence of the distance between the two excitation points on the propagation characteristics of nonlinear mixing ultrasonic waves is considered. The results show that the nonlinear parameters of the sum frequency and the difference frequency sideband increase with the increase of microcrack depth and decrease with the increase of microcrack width. Within a certain range, the sum frequency and difference frequency nonlinear parameters decrease with the increase of the distance between the two excitation points. These works lay the foundation for the engineering application of nonlinear ultrasonic Lamb wave mixing detection.

articleTitle: A Powerful Object Detection Network for Industrial Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The comprehensive task of industrial anomaly detection involves accurately classifying and precisely locating each anomaly, presenting significant practical challenges. Achieving high accuracy in both classification and localization is often difficult in a large-size image, as it requires methods to effectively balance the demands of both aspects. To overcome the challenges, this study proposes a robust object detection network YOLO-RS. In detail, we utilize the improved CSPdarknet as the backbone architecture of YOLO-RS for feature extraction. Meanwhile, this research develops a powerful neck framework of YOLO-RS for feature fusion. Furthermore, the YOLO-RS is implemented on the PCB public dataset to evaluate the proposal. Experimental results show that the YOLO-RS surpasses other state-of-the-art object detection models, achieving 93.44% mAP with only 10.15 M model parameters and reaching a fast inference speed of 73.15 FPS. These demonstrate the proposal.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Adaptive Command Filtered Backstepping Design for Uncertain Second-Order Strict-Feedback Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: A neural network-based adaptive command filtered backstepping control scheme is proposed for a class of second-order strict-feedback systems with smooth uncertain nonlinear functions. The proposed control scheme approximates the unknown smooth nonlinear function in the SFSs using RBF neural network. Unlike existing classical first-order state-space methods, command filters are introduced in the backstepping design, significantly reducing the complexity of designing control laws, overcoming the problem of “explosion of complexity”. Furthermore, the proposed scheme avoids converting a second-order system into a first-order system and allows for fewer and easier steps. Stability analysis of the closed-loop system shows that, by appropriately adjusting the design parameters, it is possible to ensure that all signals in the closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded, and this bound can be arbitrarily small.

articleTitle: Skeleton-Based Action Recognition with Adaptive Connections and Motion Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In the field of skeleton-based action recognition, ST-GCN has gained popularity because of its strong capability to model graph data and its effective use of prior knowledge regarding human joint connections. However, it faces certain challenges and limitations, such as difficulties in transferring information between non-adjacent joints and dealing with subtle variations in action speed and acceleration. To address these issues, we present a Graph Convolution Network based Adaptive connections and Motion modeling (AM-GCN). Firstly, we remove the constraints of skeleton graphs by using learnable adjacency matrices to represent dynamic connections between joints, resulting in information exchange between non-adjacent joints. Additionally, we propose a joint motion modeling technique that combines position, velocity, and acceleration information to provide richer prior knowledge about human movements, further enhancing the model's performance. Extensive experiments conducted on the NTU-RGB+D dataset show that our method performs well in skeleton-based human behavior analysis tasks, demonstrating its potential and value in practical applications.

articleTitle: Analysis Towards Deployment and Acceleration for ViT on a Lightweight RISC- V Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Vision Transformer (ViT) is the key architecture for computer vision using deep neural networks (DNNs) such as image recognition, object detection, and anomaly detection. Simultaneously, RISC- V, open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), is the center of attention, and several projects combined DNNs with RISC-V are ongoing. ViT deployment on micro-controller units (MCUs) has high expectations; however, it is a hardness challenge due to the computation cost for ViT. This paper provides a ViT implementation analysis on a small RISC-V processor for efficiency deployments and acceleration. Specif-ically, we target a CV32E40p, a 4-stage in-order 32-bit RISC- V processor core well-known for low-power and small-area. The analysis is performed from the perspective of hardware features (e.g., clock cycles, IPC, the data hazards) for the ViT components, i.e., the Patch embedding, the Layer Normalization, the Attention, and the Fully-Connected Layer. The observation results indicate the decline of instruction execution efficiency in the GEL U activation function and the Attention in addition to overwhelming computation time by matrix-multiplication operation.

articleTitle: YOLO-FG: YOLO-Based Visual Inspection for Fruits Grading
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is attracting attention because of its versatility due to research development. Progress of Advances in AI gives us the expectations to make our lives more comfortable. AI is beginning to be focused on in our personal and working lives. On the other hand, the labor shortage has recently become a serious problem in the Japanese industry. Automation of industries through AI and other IT technology is the most effective solution for this problem. Among the various industrial tasks, we focused on the inspection task because of its simplicity and the required time. However, AI has not penetrated into agriculture yet. One of the reasons is AI's model size is not appropriate to use in working. The higher detection score needs the bigger size of the model. Our research improves small AI to get higher detection score. Eventually, we aim to alleviate labor shortage problems by AI-based automatic product inspections. In this research, we develop an efficient object detection model, which is improved from YOLOX for the Visual Inspection of products. Our YOLO is optimized by focusing on the shape and size of a fruits grading. Due to our new proposal methods of convolution block(pELAN) and new IOU(eIOU), our model achieves a higher detection score than existing models. pELAN can supress to get excessive range information. It means that our model can get small defects information smoothly. eloU evaluates the center of the IoU by cutting off the circle from IoU. The above improvements improved the detection accuracy from 62.12% to 79.66% in comparison with the existing model.

articleTitle: CO Emission Prediction Model of MSWI Process Combined Sample Output and Feature Space Semi-Supervised Drift Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The municipal solid waste incineration process is susceptible to fluctuations in waste composition, equipment wear and maintenance, seasonal changes, and other variables, leading to concept drift-a time-dependent variability in pollutant emission concentration modeling data. This study introduces a semi-supervised drift detection method that integrates sample output and feature space analysis. Initially, an unsupervised approach based on principal component analysis identifies concept drift samples in the feature space. Subsequently, pseudo-truth values for these concept drift samples are labeled using a semi-supervised method based on time-difference learning in the sample output space. Detection of concept drift is then performed using the Page-Hinkley method. Finally, the LSTM model is updated with both new and historical samples. Experimental results based on real CO process dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Distributed Nash Equilibrium Seeking of Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems Under Unknown False Data Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper investigates resilient adaptively distributed Nash Equilibrium (NE) seeking problems for noncooperative games of double-integrator players under malicious attacks, i.e., false data injection (FDI) attacks. Different from distributed NE seeking in many existing literature under ideal environments, it is challenging to achieve the NE seeking under unknown and unbounded FDI attacks. An attack-resilient NE seeking architecture that is distributed, is established by means of the consensus-based gradient play together with an attack identifier to deal with the impacts of FDI attacks. Another key characteristic is that malicious FDI attacks are allowed to be completely unknown and unbounded. The global asymptotic convergence of the proposed distributed NE seeking algorithm to-ward the NE is guaranteed. Lastly, numerical simulation results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Research Progress and Key Technology Analysis in Cooperative Control of Dual Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: To meet the intricate demands of modern industries, multi-robot cooperative control systems offer broad applications, robust fault tolerance, and high efficiency. This research proposes trajectory compensation and digital twin technology as remedies for challenging collaborative planning, low real-time and accuracy, limited model accuracy, and inadequate planning of complicated tasks in dual-robot cooperative control. Trajectory compensation has the potential to increase task efficiency, boost environmental adaptability, and maximize cooperative performance; digital twin technology is essential for real-time monitoring and prediction, cooperative control strategy optimization, fault diagnosis and prevention, and maintenance cost savings.

articleTitle: An Alternative Dual Control Approach for Auto-Optimization in Uncertain Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of dual control for exploitation and exploration (DCEE) for auto-optimization in uncertain environments. Different from existing adaptive control methods, an exploration effect is additionally considered in the DCEE framework. By providing an alternative dual control approach, the system output can be driven to the estimated nominal value and the uncertainty of the predicted optimal operational condition can be reduced. The convergence analysis of optimality tracking process of general linear systems is established using the DCEE framework. Simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the developed DCEE.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Model of NOx Emission Concentration in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Municipalsolid waste incineration (MSWI) has significant advantages in terms of harmlessness, reduction, and resource utilization. Pollution emission control is a major problem in the operation of MSWI plants. Therefore, to understand the formation, reduction, and combustion mechanism of NOx in the furnace, this article proposed a numerical simulation model based on coupling several software. First, according to the typical grate MSWI process, the relevant reaction mechanism of NOx in the furnace is described. Then, according to the grate and gas reaction mechanism of an MSWI plant in Beijing, the reaction region is divided, and the numerical simulation model is constructed based on the benchmark parameters of the actual MSWI plant. Finally, the effectiveness of the numeral simulation model is verified by experiments. These results can provide support for the pollution optimization control of the actual MSWI process.

articleTitle: Multitarget Robust Deep Stochastic Configuration Network Parameter Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: To improve the model accuracy of deep stochastic configuration network (DSCN) in multitarget robust parameter modeling tasks, this paper presents a multitarget robust DSCN modeling method. This method expands the hidden layer output matrix by optimizing the network model structure and exploiting the correlation between multiple targets to improve the modeling quality. The model output weights are optimized by constructing a sparse weighted robust loss function that combines the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L2$</tex>,1-norm with the Laplace kernel function, which reduces the model's sensitivity to abnormal training data. Experimental tests are performed on multitarget benchmark datasets to validate the modeling performance of the method. The experimental results show that the multitarget parameter model constructed via the proposed method has advantages in terms of accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Design of Recursive Filtering Scheme via An Improved Weighted Try-Once Discard Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the recursive filtering (RF) problem for stochastic multi-rate (MR) systems, where the information transmission is regulated by an improved weighted try-once-discard protocol (IWTODP). In order to reduce communication overhead and mitigate network congestion, the IWTODP is firstly proposed and designed to schedule the order of data transmission from the sensors. The main objective of this paper is to design a new RF scheme to minimize the upper bound (UB) on the filtering error (FE) covariance in each iteration step in the presence of IWTODP and MR sampling. In particular, an iterative way is given to provide the expression form of the gain of RF. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed RF method is illustrated through simulation example.

articleTitle: Image Recognition Empowers Intelligent Analysis of Industrial Drawings
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper develops a specialized drawing data management software to address the challenges of information management and the application of drawing data in industrial production. This software integrates image segmentation algorithms based on OpenCV and text recognition algorithms based on CnOCR. It is designed to process two types of drawing data: part drawings and assembly drawings. First, the PDF files are converted into images. For part drawings, edge detection algorithms in OpenCV are utilized for segmentation, and recognition algorithms are employed to accurately locate and remove numbers, ultimately generating quality inspection diagrams. A text recognition algorithm is utilized for assembly drawings to extract data from the drawings, followed by feature processing and analysis to extract information regarding all components depicted in the drawings. The software also incorporates a feature for searching by component shape to facilitate the retrieval of drawing data. The findings suggest that the algorithm effectively recognizes drawing data, automates data statistics and quality inspection processes, elevates intelligent drawing data management, and holds substantial practical utility.

articleTitle: Incremental Learning based Broad Canonical Correlation Analysis Network for Industrial Process Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper proposes an incremental learning based broad canonical correlation analysis network (ILBCCAN) to address the time-consuming problem of deep learning models in training process. It uses canonical correlation window, mapping window, and enhancement window to extract the correlation and nonlinear structure between variables, thus improves the feature extraction capability. Moreover, it continues to maintain the advantage of the broad learning system in terms of time overhead by using a pseudo-inverse strategy to determine the network parameters, which greatly reduces the training time. In addition, the proposed ILBCCAN model has an incremental learning capability. In scenarios where high accuracy is required or where the network structure needs to be adjusted online for real-time updating, the number of node parameters is flexibly determined by dynamically adding enhancement nodes within the incremental window, which avoids the need to retrain the entire network from scratch for achieving the desired level. Finally, the ILBCCAN model is used for fault monitoring. Case studies show that the proposed model outperforms other fault monitoring methods based on Tennessee Eastman benchmark.

articleTitle: Temporal Graph Convolutional Network-Based Fault Detection Method for the Two-Wheeled Self-Balancing Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The fault detection method based on graph neural networks has been widely applied. However, few of these methods consider the dynamic characteristics and prior knowledge of control systems, resulting in limited usage for fault detection in control systems. To address this, this article proposes a fault detection method based on temporal graph convolutional neural network (T-GCN) and multi-layer perceptron (MLP), which is applicable to general linear dynamic control systems. The proposed method first constructs a relational graph based on prior knowledge of the control system and utilizes T-GCN to extract spatio-temporal relationships between various state variables and control input signals within the system. Then, a MLP integrates the extracted information to detect whether the control system has experienced faults. Finally, a two-wheeled self-balancing vehicle is utilized to test the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach could achieve high-precision detection of sensor faults within the system.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Neural Networks-Based Intelligent Tracking Control for Flexible-Joint Industry Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Due to the unstructured environment and the complex target tasks, the traditional mechanism and control theory are not able to meet the requirements of the real-time high-accuracy control of the environment-adaptive robot systems. This paper focuses on flexible-joint industry robotic manipulator, which can effectively resist external forces and reduce the vibration. Fuzzy neural networks-based intelligent control is designed to achieve precise trajectory tracking while address dynamic uncertainty issues for flexible-joint i ndustry robotic manipulator. Subsequently, the ultimately uniformly boundedness of the closed-loop system is proven through Lyapunov's direct method. With the careful choice of parameters, the system's states can converge to a small neighborhood close to zero. Finally, several necessary experiments on Baxter platform are provided to validate the proposed control method. The superiority of this control method is shown through its comparison with both PD control and neural network control techniques.

articleTitle: Remote Fault Diagnosis Method for Traction Drive Systems Based on Domain-Adapted Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Rail trains are a vital component of railway passenger transport and regional economic development. The traction drive system serves as the power source for rail trains. Due to the complex composition of system components and the working environment being affected by coupled multi-physical fields such as electric, thermal, and magnetic influences, long-term operation often leads to wear, aging, and sudden anomalies in certain components. Failure to perform timely maintenance can result in significant economic losses and casualties. Thus, rapid and efficient fault diagnosis of the traction drive system is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of rail trains. Existing fault diagnosis methods for traction drive systems can be divided into online and remote diagnostics. Online diagnostics typically rely on structured time-series data for analysis. However, as the system continues to operate, a significant amount of unstructured knowledge about faults accumulates, which is vital for enhancing the depth and breadth of fault diagnosis, yet online diagnostic methods are unable to effectively utilize this knowledge. Traditional remote diagnostics mainly involve experts using their experiential knowledge combined with fault logs, maintenance manuals, etc. However, expert consultations heavily depend on human experience, and the storage methods for fault logs are flat, lacking intuitiveness and difficult to query, which leads to inefficient utilization of unstructured knowledge. Therefore, there is an urgent need to introduce new methods to fully utilize unstructured fault knowledge and improve the efficiency of fault diagnosis. Knowledge graphs are a type of semantic network-based knowledge base, primarily extracting entities and relationships from unstructured knowledge for storage in a directed graph of nodes and edges. In the context of remote fault diagnosis systems, the introduction of knowledge graphs can standardize and unify the storage and expression of unstructured knowledge such as fault corpora and expert knowledge dispersed across various documents. This enables efficient knowledge querying and reasoning, which is critical for enhancing the utilization of unstructured knowledge, reducing dependency on expert experience, and ultimately improving diagnostic efficiency and shortening maintenance decision-making times. Currently, knowledge graphs have been widely applied in many research areas such as medicine, industrial manufacturing, and agriculture, showcasing their potential applications. However, most of these applications only consider the knowledge graph construction process within their specific fields, with few studies reported on using knowledge graphs for remote fault diagnosis in rail train traction drive systems. Moreover, the information extraction stage of building system knowledge graphs faces issues with low accuracy, especially given the diverse sources of fault corpora and the relatively rare domain-specific terminology in traction drive systems, making traditional knowledge graph construction methods challenging to apply directly. In summary, this paper proposes a remote fault diagnosis method based on domain-adapted knowledge graphs. Firstly, it introduces a domain-adapted segmentation method to construct a system fault lexicon, addressing the issue of large errors in splitting specialized phrases under a general lexicon. Secondly, it addresses the lack of interactivity in traditional information extraction processes causing disconnection between subtasks by introducing a dual BiLSTM combination method for information extraction, which shares features between entity extraction and relationship extraction to enhance their potential interconnection. The paper's experiments use long-term operational fault logs from a specific train model as data sources to validate the overall method's effectiveness; it also analyzes the effects of each component of the proposed method through ablation studies. Finally, based on the proposed method, a remote fault diagnosis system has been established, offering a new solution for rapid and efficient maintenance decision-making.

articleTitle: An Integrated Adversarial Fine-tuning Method for Improving the Safety of Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Fault diagnosis is one of the key parts in the industrial field, and the current intelligent fault diagnosis meth-ods based on machine learning have achieved a wide range of applications. Although more research exists on this issue, less research has been done on the security of fault diagnosis methods. The security vulnerability of machine learning brings potential risks to fault diagnosis, which may lead to unanticipated property damage and casualties. Current defense methods based on adversarial training cause a degradation of standard accuracy while improving the robustness of machine learning models, which hinders the application of adversarial defense in the field of fault diagnosis. To address this issue, this study proposes an integrated adversarial fine-tuning method, which generates rep-resentative adversarial samples by integrating multiple methods, and uses the adversarial samples to fine-tune the vulnerable fault diagnosis model, thus realizing the improvement of the adversarial robustness of fault diagnosis while guaranteeing the standard accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method in this study is demonstrated through well-designed experiments based on publicly available datasets.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Wastewater Treatment Process Based on Improved Fast Non-Dominated Sorting Algorithm with Hybrid Crossover Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: With the increasingly serious water pollution problems, wastewater treatment process has become a hot spot in today's research. The key issue of wastewater treatment process is to achieve the optimization of the system's energy consumption and cost reduction under the premise of meeting the effluent water quality standards, so as to achieve the purpose of “maintaining quality and reducing consumption”. The traditional fast non-dominated sequential genetic (NSGA II) algorithm uses Simulated Binary Crossover (SBX) to generate offspring to deal with the optimization problem, which may have the problems of limited search range and unstable evolutionary process, etc. In this paper, we propose a hybrid crossover algorithm based on SBX to generate offspring. In this paper, an improved fast non-dominated sorting algorithm based on hybrid crossover operator (MIX-NSGA II) is proposed to solve the above problems, and by introducing Normal Distribution Crossover (NDX) in the crossover process, MIX-NSGA II is proposed to strengthen the global search capability, improve the convergence speed and algorithmic running speed, and obtain higher quality optimized solutions.

articleTitle: DRL-Based Resource Scheduling for Control System in Heterogeneous Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: We investigate the scheduling problem of control tasks in heterogeneous environments. We measure the computational resource required for linear quadratic regulators (LQR) and model the scheduling problem as the bin packing problem. We formulate the bin packing problem as a Markov Decision Process. In the Markov Decision Process, we generate two action subspaces within the action space and propose an algorithm called DARL based on deep reinforcement learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the DARL has improved training efficiency and learning performance compared to base-lines, effectively addressing the challenges of resource scheduling of control tasks in heterogeneous environments.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Nonlinear Systems Using Generalized Associated Linear Equations (GALEs)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: For a weakly nonlinear system described by Volterra series, if the nonlinear differential equation (NDE) model of the system is unique, the nonlinear auto-regressive with exogenous input (NARX) model identified based on the input and output data of that system is not unique. Fortunately, the NDE model and the NARX model of the same nonlinear system have unique frequency domain representations, e.g., generalized frequency response functions (GFRFs), so these two models also have the same nonlinear output response spectrum. And the generalized associated linear equations (GALEs) theory can be used to directly calculate the arbitrary order nonlinear output response of the system according to the parameters of the NDE model or the NARX model. Therefore, this paper proposes a parameter identification method of the NDE model for the nonlinear system based on GALEs. Firstly, the NARX model of the system is identified according to the input and output data generated by the NDE model of the system with unknown parameters. Secondly, the GALEs of the NDE model containing the unknown parameters are determined. Finally, the unknown parameters in the NDE model are identified based on the principle that the NDE model and the NARX model of the same system have the same nonlinear output response spectrum. The method is convenient and effective, and provides a new idea for parameter identification of NDE models of nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: An Integrated MPC Decision-Making Method Based on MDP for Autonomous Driving in Urban Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The decision-making module plays a critical role in autonomous vehicles (AVs). There are two main challenges in decision-making for autonomous driving: accurately predicting and reliably reacting to evolving environments. This work addresses these challenges by implementing an integrated decision-making method that merges the Markov decision process (MDP) with model predictive control (MPC) structure. This method ensures that optimal and safe decision actions can be generated in real-time by solving the MPC optimization problem, subject to conditions such as environmental evolution, dynamics of continuous systems, MDP state transitions, and safety constraints. To validate the decision-making method, an information-rich urban crossroad scenario, including traffic signals, other vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, has been considered for performance testing. The effectiveness and reliability of the decision-making method have been demonstrated through these highly variable urban environments.

articleTitle: Network Based Control System Design Optimization for Buck Circuits Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Optimization of control systems for power electronic systems using evolutionary algorithms has gained significant attention in current research. However, the effectiveness of such methods heavily relies on the accuracy of initial data collection, often leading to prolonged time consumption with higher precision. This paper presents an approach for optimizing control systems of Buck circuits by integrating BP neural networks to address both data accuracy and time efficiency using genetic algorithm. Initially, data corresponding to controller parameters and system indicators are collected. Subsequently, BP neural networks are utilized to model the relationship between multiple controller parameters and control indicators. After that, the genetic algorithm is employed to optimize system controller parameters continuously. Finally, the proposed method is implemented in a Matlab/Simulink control system, and its efficacy is validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Skip-CBAM Based Unsupervised Anomaly Detection of Fused Magnesia Furnace
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Abnormal ultra-high temperature semi-molten conditions in a fused magnesia furnace (FMF) can lead to furnace leakage. To ensure high detection performance, existing models require sufficient expert-labeled training data for supervised learning. However, the above model has limited ability to identify unknown abnormal working conditions, and label production is time-consuming and expensive. This paper suggests an unsupervised detection method based on skip-connected generative adversarial network (GAN) to address this issue. Specifically, to adapt to the strong interference caused by irregular changes in images caused by irregular water mist and flicker scenes, existing methods remove interference through multi-step processing for detection, which is difficult to apply in practice. In contrast, we use a reconstruction model of convolutional block attention module (CBAM) with skip connections for end-to-end computation, which improves performance while being more concise. This method determines abnormal areas through reconstruction and distinguishes abnormal working conditions by comparing abnormal scores. Finally, this method is compared with existing unsupervised and supervised methods on actual FMF images, and the application results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Health State Estimation Based on Hierarchical Feature Construction and Adaptive Gated Sequence Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: State of health (SOH) estimation is vital in ensuring lithium-ion battery management systems' safe and stable operation (BMS). Data-driven methods are widely used to estimate SOH; however, existing methods often suffer from fixed or excessively high feature dimensions, impacting the model's adjustability and applicability. In this regard, this paper first proposes a layered knee-point strategy based on the charging voltage curve, which reduces the complexity of feature extraction. Then, a new hybrid framework called the Adaptive Gated Sequence Network (AGSN) model was proposed. The model integrates the Independent Recurrent Neural Network (IndRNN) layers, Active State Tracking Long Short-Term Memory (AST-LSTM) layers, and Adaptive Gating Mechanism (AGM) layers. By integrating a multi-layer structure and an adaptive gating mechanism, the SOH prediction performance was significantly improved. Finally, batteries under different operating conditions were tested using the NASA battery dataset. The results show that the AGSN model demonstrates higher accuracy and robustness in battery SOH estimation, with estimation errors consistently within 1%.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of A Stick-Slip Type Dielectric Elastomer Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs) are a class of promising smart materials-based actuators, that show a sandwich structure with two compliant electrodes and an elastomer membrane.
