When DEAs are subjected to an input voltage, it causes an increase in area and a decrease in the thickness of the elastomer membrane. In recent years, numerous DEAs have been developed, yet they frequently encounter challenges such as low actuation speed, restricted directional motion, and limited strain capacity. Therefore, a stick-slip dielectric elastomer motor (SSDEM) is proposed with the stick-slip mechanism. In this paper, the overall structure and the actuating unit design of SSDEM are introduced in detail, and how to convert the telescopic motion of the DE membrane into stick-slip motion is explained. Then, a dynamic analysis and modeling of the SSDEM actuating unit are conducted. Depending on different motion modes, the SSDEM is classified into two operating modes: the scanning mode, which can be utilized for precision operation, and the stick-slip mode, suitable for fast actuation. Finally, a displacement measuring platform is built to test the motion performance of the SSDEM. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the designed SSDEM in motion performance.

articleTitle: The Experimental Research On Off-axis Digital Holography Recording And Reconstruction Based On MATLAB Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This article first analyzes the two-step imaging process in optical holography, namely wavefront recording and wavefront reconstruction. According to the relationship of the four diffraction components in the spatial spectrum of the off-axis digital holography diffraction process, the minimum angle is derived between the object light and the reference light of the off-axis digital holography. According to the sampling theorem, the maximum angle is derived between the object light and the reference light in off-axis digital holography. The mathematical derivation of holography algorithm is introduced based on these foundations. In the experiment, a light path system was used to study the method of eliminating zero order in off-axis digital holograms by recording reference light at different angles to the X-axis or Y-axis, while improving the image resolution of off-axis digital holographic reconstruction. Secondly, the off-axis digital holographic recording optical path was constructed to eliminate zero order holographic imaging by comparing the reference light with different angles of the X-axis or Y-axis. The current Fresnel approximation reconstruction algorithm is analyzed and verified by simulation. The results indicate that the S-FFT (Single-Fast Fourier Transform) reconstructed image undergoes periodic changes from overlap to separation, and then from separation to overlap.

articleTitle: Flue Gas Oxygen Content Modeling Approach Based on BPNN and LRDT in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Flue gas oxygen content is one of the key controlled variables of municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process. And it is closely related to the combustion efficiency and pollutant emission. At present, there are few reports on flue gas oxygen content model as the controlled object. The article proposes a flue gas oxygen content modeling method based on the fusion of back propagation neural network (BPNN) and linear regression decision tree (LRDT). Firstly, the BPNN model is used to construct the main model. Then, LRDT is used to construct the compensation model by using the error of the of main model as the output. Finally, the fusion output is obtained by summarizing the LRDT and BPNN model. Experimental results based on actual operating data of a MSWI plant in Beijing shows the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Particulate Matter Generation Inside Furnace of Municipal Solid Waste Incineration on Benchmark Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) processes produce particulate matter that can cause air pollution. Understanding the formation mechanism of particulate matter (PM) inside the furnace, in terms of pollutant generation sources, is crucial for pollution reduction and optimal control. This article proposes a numerical simulation model to analyze PM generation inside the MSWI furnace under benchmark operating conditions, by coupling several software tools. Initially, the MSWI process is analyzed to identify key variables affecting PM generation. Subsequently, a numerical simulation model of PM generation in the incinerator, integrating FLIC and FLUENT software, is developed. The flow field distribution and PM concentration under benchmark conditions are then analyzed. The effectiveness of this method is validated using actual data from an MSWI plant in Beijing, providing practical insights for reducing PM concentrations through process improvements and optimal control.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Active Disturbance Rejection Control Method for Hydrogen Production by Alkaline Electrolysis of Green Electricity
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Green electrolysis of water for hydrogen production has a very wide application prospect because of its ability to utilize renewable energy to produce hydrogen. However, in the process of hydrogen production by green power, the temperature at the working point of the system fluctuates continuously due to the strong volatility of renewable energy, so a linear self-resistant controller (LADRC) based on the Nash Equilibrium Quantum Particle Swarm (NEQPSO) algorithm is proposed. First, the temperature control process of the green power hydrogen production system is analyzed, and the LADRC control method is proposed for the perturbations in the process. Second, the Nash equilibrium is integrated into the quantum particle swarm algorithm to optimize the parameters of the linear self-oscillating controller, and the optimized parameters are applied to the control system. The results of the simulation indicate that the overshoot of the LADRC method by 10.39% was reduced due to the perturbation. The rapidity also improved by 17.60%, demonstrating a favorable control effect.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Study of the Effect of Nitrogen and Oxygen Content on Membrane Fouling Based on MSCA-Fused-MBConv
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Membrane fouling has become the main factor hindering the development of membrane biological wastewater treatment technology. The factors have strong coupling, nonlinearity and time lag, and the content of nitrogen and oxygen in the pool is an important factor directly affecting the development of membrane fouling. Therefore, this paper proposed to use the Multi-scale Spatial and Channel-wise Attention (MSCA) to improve the diagnostic network of the Fused-Mobile inverted Bottleneck Convolution (Fused-MBConv), followed by the stable operation of MBR. Firstly, this paper employed the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method to identify ammonia nitrogen indices with strong correlations that directly impacted membrane fouling. Secondly, the filtered time-series data were transformed using the Markov Transition Field (MTF) method, which preserved the integration of data features and temporal characteristics. Thirdly, the MSCA attention mechanism was utilized to optimize the structure of Fused-MBConv in EfficientNetV2. Finally, through ablation experiments and comparisons with other related networks, it was concluded that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 0.9953 and maintained an average running time of 2.13 seconds. Additionally, 5-fold cross-validation experiments confirmed that the MSCA-Fused-MBConv diagnostic network demonstrated strong robustness and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm for Scheduling of Steelmaking and Continuous Casting Processes Considering Earliness/Tardiness Penalty*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The production scheduling for steelmaking and continuous casting operations involves the allocation of each heat to specific equipment at various stages within the steelmaking process. Refinement and continuous casting are performed in accordance with the casting plans formulated by the planner and simultaneously determine the production sequence and start/finish time of heats on each equipment. The production scheduling for steel refining and continuous casting processes in this paper is modeled as a flexible job shop scheduling problem. Aiming at just-in-time production of orders, we formulate a mixed-integer programming model (MILP) and introduce a genetic algorithm to address the issue. The validity of the model and the efficiency of the algorithm are confirmed through real-world instances of production scheduling challenges.

articleTitle: Infrared and Visible Image Fusion with Deformable Cross-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This article introduces a novel fusion framework based on Swin Transformer and deformable attention, primarily designed for infrared and visible image fusion. Our approach comprises four components: feature extraction, an intra-domain fusion module, a cross-domain fusion module, and feature reconstruction. The core innovation lies in the Deformable Cross-Attention module, which integrates cross attention and deformable attention within the Swin Transformer architecture. This design enables our model to effectively fuse relevant feature information from different domains. Moreover, the integration of deformable attention also enhances the flexibility of our attention mechanism, enabling it to focus on data more effectively. The incorporated Swin Transformer's window mechanism significantly reduces the computational cost of attention calculations. The shift window mechanism further enables our model to accommodate images of arbitrary sizes. Additionally, we employ a weighted sum of SSIM loss, texture loss, and intensity loss during training to ensure our network preserves both rich texture information and intensity information. Experimental results demonstrate that our model not only outperforms other state-of-the-art models in terms of quantitative metrics such as SSIM and Qabf’ but also exhibits superior fusion performance in terms of the visual quality.

articleTitle: Residual Multi-Attention U-Net for Image Segmentation in Heavy Plate Hot Rolling Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Accurately segmenting hot rolling heavy plate images is challenging due to mist occlusion and varying visual features caused by different plate temperatures during the hot rolling process. This difficulty consequently affects the subsequent contour detection of the heavy plates. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Residual Multi-Attention U-Net network for segmenting hot rolling heavy plate images. This method effectively handles mist and color interference in the heavy plate regions by incorporating attention modules in both spatial and channel dimensions. By leveraging features extracted through a pre-trained ResNet, the segmentation model's resistance to interference and robustness are significantly enhanced. Extensive experiments were conducted on real-world hot rolling heavy plate image data, comparing the proposed multi-attention U-Net method with standard approaches such as U-Net, SegFormer, SwinTransformer, HRNet, PSPNet, and U-next. The experimental results demonstrate that the multi-attention U-Net method achieves superior IoU accuracy in steel plate image segmentation while maintaining real-time performance.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Graph Fusion Transformer for Long-term Water Quality Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Over the past decades of rapid development, the global water pollution problem has become prominent. Accurate water quality prediction can detect the trend and anomaly of water quality changes in advance, thereby taking timely measures to avoid the occurrence of water quality problems. Traditional statistical methods for water quality prediction make it difficult to capture the complex relationship between multiple variables and deep learning models make it difficult to capture temporal dependence and spatial correlation of the water quality simultaneously. To solve the above problems, this work proposes an adaptive and dynamic graph fusion water quality prediction model based on a spatiotemporal attention mechanism named Spatlal-Temporal Graph Fusion Transformer (STGFT). It in-tegrates a spatial attention encoder (SAE), a temporal attention encoder (TAE), an adaptive dynamic adjacency matrix generator (ADMG), and a multi-graph fusion layer. Among them, SAE and TAE are adopted to capture the spatial correlations and temporal characteristics among different water quality monitoring stations, respectively. ADMG generates adaptive and dynamic adjacency matrices to reflect potential spatial relationships in the river net-work. Experimental results with real-life water quality datasets demonstrate that STGFT outperforms current state-of-the-art models regarding prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Priors-Informed Machine Learning for Dynamic System Modelling: Mecanum Wheel as an Example
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: An accurate dynamic model holds critical significance for model based applications such as state estimation, system control, monitoring and optimization. While first principles based dynamic modelling allows for clear interpretability, it faces difficulties for complex systems under uncertainties. Purely data-driven machine learning based black box modelling is easy to implement but has low interpretability, poor generalization and often demands extensive data. This study advocates hybrid modelling seamlessly integrating prior knowledge into machine learning for better modelling performance. Specifically, we focus on assessing the impacts of different levels of model priors on machine learning based modelling performance utilizing the Neural Ordinary Differential Equation framework. Comparative simulations on a Mecanum wheel mobile robot show that an increased level of prior modelling information effectively enhances the modelling performance.

articleTitle: A 3D Spiral-Zigzag Gas Leakage Source Search Algorithm Based on Olfaction and Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Accidents such as fires and chemical leakage, which occur from time to time, seriously endanger public safety. The use of robot to discover and track the source of gas/chemical plume can replace traditional manual search, greatly reducing the risk and cost of search and improving efficiency. Most of the existing gas leakage source search methods are applied in two-dimensional environments, and for the scenarios where the plume is visible, the efficiency of searching and the success rate of source localization only relying on the olfaction is usually low. To this end, this paper proposes a plume finding and tracing method based on olfaction and vision with a drone in 3D outdoor environments. In the plume finding phase, olfactory information is combined with visual object detection in the 3D Spiral algorithm to improve plume finding efficiency. During the plume tracing phase, the drone performs a 3D Zigzag motion to rapidly approach the source of the gas leakage. If the plume is lost during tracing, the 3D Spiral algorithm, which combines olfactory and visual information, is used again in local area with a view to find the plume again. Experimental and simulation results show that the efficiency of plume finding can be significantly improved by using visual object detection for the plume, and the proposed plume finding and tracing method combining olfactory and visual information has high search efficiency and success rate.

articleTitle: Detachment Force Modeling of Micro Suction Tape Based on A Three- Layer Trajectory Filtering Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The detachment force is a crucial metric for evaluating the performance of climbing robots, a larger detachment force signifi-cantly impacts system stability. Establishing a detachment force model can guide climbing robots to minimize this force, ensuring stable detachment. However, current climbing robots primarily focus on functional implementation without considering the influ-ence of adhesive material detachment force, especially for high-adhesion dry adhesives like Micro suction tape(MST). To address this issue, this paper proposes a method for modeling the detachment force of MST. First, a setup was designed to capture video data of detachment angles and speeds during the detachment process, and a three-dimensional force sensor was used to collect detachment force data. Real-time detachment trajectories of the MST were extracted using visual segmentation and detection al-gorithms. A three-layer trajectory filtering strategy was employed to remove interference from the trajectories, thereby obtaining accurate detachment angles and speeds. The genetic algorithm was then used for parameter identification of the detachment force model to determine unknown physical parameters. Ultimately, the MST detachment force model was derived, with a maximum error of 0.234 N and a maximum mean squared error of 0.0073 compared to the actual detachment force data.

articleTitle: Odor Source Search with a Wolf Pack Algorithm via Multi-UAV in Outdoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Concerning the problem of odor source search with robots in a large outdoor environment, an odor source search method based on the improved wolf pack algorithm (IWPA) is proposed, in which each wolf corresponds to an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The environment is firstly traversed by the UAVs in partitions by using rectangular wave- shaped paths. Once odor plume is detected by any UAV, the WPA is applied to guide the UAVs towards the odor source. Considering the limited number of UAVs, in order to improve the utilization rate of UAVs, the wolf pack is simplified into two roles: the alpha wolf and other wolves. Meanwhile, to avoid collisions between UAVs and enable UAVs to fully sample around the suspected target position, a besieging algorithm based on a virtual force field is designed to calculate next flight direction for the UAVs. During this period, the odor source position is determined by the alpha wolf which is constantly elected by comparing the fitness values of all wolves. Simulation results show that the IWPA method can find the odor source in short time without falling into local extremum, demonstrating good convergence and being suitable for odor source search tasks in outdoor environments.

articleTitle: An Anti-Overlap Object Feature Weighted Fusion Detector for X-Ray Prohibited Item Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Security checkpoints equipped with X-ray scanners play a crucial role in ensuring public safety by inspecting luggage for prohibited items. However, even trained professionals can easily make errors when manually inspecting X-ray images. To assist in manual inspection, direct application of object detection methods to X-rays can lead to false positives and false negatives due to overlapping objects. To address this issue, this paper proposes an object feature weighted fusion detector (OFWF-Detector) for X-ray prohibited item detection. The OFWF-Detector utilizes an object confidence mask selection (OCMS) mechanism to filter overlapping features, improving detection accuracy. Experimental results on the PIX ray dataset demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces false positives and false negatives, achieving superior performance compared to traditional methods. Specifically, the OFWF-Detector enhances the detection of small objects in overlapping scenarios by 12.9 % in terms of APs from Tab. I, showcasing its effectiveness in all the challenges posed by overlapping objects in X-ray images. These findings highlight the potential of the OFWF-Detector to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of security screening systems, contributing to improved public safety in high-traffic areas.

articleTitle: Early Damage Detection Based on FRF-CNN-BiLSTM Model and NOFRF
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Early-stage damage has become a potential source of catastrophic structural failures, therefore, the development of effective early damage detection methods is crucial. The nonlinear output frequency response function (NOFRF) and related indexes can be considered effective detection tools. NOFRF is typically determined using an established nonlinear auto-regressive with exogenous inputs (NARX) model. However, the hyperparameters in the NARX model are difficult to determine, and the identification accuracy cannot be guaranteed. Model based on the frequency response function (FRF) can capture the linear relationship between the system's input and output channels. However, most actual systems exhibit characteristics of nonlinear behavior, leading to prediction errors in the FRF model's responses. Inspired by the powerful learning capabilities of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, this paper proposes a hybrid modeling strategy. This strategy combines the FRF model with the CNN-BiLSTM model to obtain a more accurate response of the nonlinear system. Through simulation studies using two different types of excitation signals (harmonic signals and sweep signals), NOFRF and related indexes can be accurately estimated, thereby enabling the detection of early damage. The effectiveness and generality of the proposed method have been validated.

articleTitle: Decentralized Adaptive Pseudo-Inverse Control for Output Constrained Systems on Giant Magnetostrictive Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Rigid smart material actuators, such as giant magnetostrictive actuators (GMAs), are characterized by high energy density, fast response speed and large mechanical output. It is widely used in the fields of industrial robotics, precision positioning and microelectronic systems. This paper proposes a decentralized adaptive pseudo inverse control scheme based on neural networks for a class of nonlinear time-delay systems with output constraints, which reduces the impact of hysteresis on the system. The main research content includes 1) the pseudo-inverse control programme is proposed to overcome the hysteresis phenomenon in the actuator 2) with the help of RBFNN, finite coverage primitives and potential Lyapunov function, the output-constrained control problem of interconnected time-lagged nonlinear systems is solved by designing an approximator for the time-lagged nonlinear function; and 3) an experimental platform for precision control based on a three-axis GMA is designed, and the scheme is verified for the control performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Knowledge Inheritance Graph Neural Network for Tobacco Pest Time-Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The quality of tobacco raw materials is the decisive factor affecting the quality of cigarette products. The monitoring and forecasting of tobacco pest distribution in the factory is crucial in preventing the invasion of tobacco pests into the raw materials, thereby mitigating potential economic losses. However, traditional time series forecasting methods fail to deal with the multi-level spatial characteristics within the tobacco pest distribution data, therefore leading to poor forecasting performance. In this work, a multi-level knowledge inheritance graph network (MKIGN) is proposed to handle this problem. First, by creating virtual variables, a workshop-level dataset and a district-level dataset were generated from the original point-level dataset. Then, a multi-level graph network structure with an integrated knowledge inheritance strategy is designed, which will be applied to the two newly constructed datasets to capture the multi-level spatial characteristics of the tobacco pest distribution data. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are illustrated on a real tobacco pest distribution dataset.

articleTitle: Fractional-Order Control for Composite Silicone Dielectric Elastomer Actuated Motion System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In this paper a new dynamical system model is constructed and a fractional-order control scheme is proposed to deal with the high precision control problem of composite silicone rubber dielectric elastomer actuator (DEA). The main contributions are summarized as: 1) the strong nonlinearity behavior of the DEA is described by constructing a new Kelvin-Voigt and 3-parameter Mooney-Rivlin model. Then it is validated through open-loop input-outnut experiments. 2) a new fractional-order dynamical model of DEA is constructed and a corresponding fractional-order controller is proposed. Then a satisfactory tracking control performance is achieved. Finally comparison experiments are implemented on the constructed dielectric elastomer actuated platform to show the advantages of the proposed fractional-order control scheme

articleTitle: Detection Method for Flotation Tailings Ash Content Based on Regularized Stochastic Configuration Networks Dynamic Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The ash content of flotation tailings is a crucial parameter in flotation operations. This paper proposes a ash content predicting method via capturing infrared backscattered light from flotation tailings with multiple light scattering instruments in response to the current challenges of online ash content detection technologies, such as high costs, environmental pollution, and the discrepancy between the costs of detection principle technology and accuracy. The linear relationship between light intensity and concentration is established by Mie theory when the ash content is inversely proportional to light intensity. Based on this relationship, a tailings ash content prediction model which taking concentration correction into account is developed. In this study, various ash content tailings with different concentration ranging from 0 g/L to 80 g/L were selected to research the coupling effects of backscattered light intensity with ash content and concentration. The industrial experimental results show that the L-RSC model obtained by combining the linear model and nonlinear RSC model based on regularized stochastic configuration network has good performance. The model achieved a 68.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of detected values within an acceptable error margin of (δ<1.0%, along with an average absolute error (MAE) of 0.54, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.69, a coefficient of determination (R2) of 99.21 % and a detection duration of 5 minutes. This study aims to propose an offline, passive, and cost-effective detection method for coal tailings and establish a data-driven prediction model to facilitate the detection of ash content in flotation tailings, thereby opening up new avenues in this field.

articleTitle: Real-Time Caustic Ratio Control in Alumina Digestion Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Due to the lag time in the alumina digestion process (ALDP), traditional control methods that depend on delayed measurements often struggle to maintain the optimal caustic ratio, which is crucial for achieving optimal performance. This paper proposes a novel intelligent operational control method to address this challenge. Our multi-stage framework employs a fuzzy inference system (FIS) to generate an initial setpoint based on process knowledge. Subsequently, a bi-directional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) network predicts the endpoint caustic ratio, assessing the validity of the initial setpoint. Finally, a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) adjustor refines the setpoint in real-time based on the predicted and target values. Validated with industrial data, this method significantly improves the qualification rate of the caustic ratio compared to manual operation. It demonstrates the effectiveness of DDPG for real-time setpoint adjustment, leading to improved product quality in the ALDP.

articleTitle: Identification of Superheat Degree for Aluminum Electrolysis Based on Feature-Guide Deep Variational Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Identification of Superheat Degree (SD) plays a critical role in decision-making of aluminum electrolysis process. With the development of industrial information technology, multimodal data can be collected from aluminum electrolysis cell, such as process data, flame hole images. To fully make use of process data and flame hole images, this paper proposes a SD identification method based on feature-guide deep variational autoencoder. According to flame hole images, the static features and dynamic features of flame hole video related to superheat are extracted. Feature-guide deep variational auto encoder is proposed to extract the deep features from flame hole images by feature alignment between the static-dynamic features and the deep features. Then, Fuzzy inference network is constructed to obtain the SD status according to process data, static-dynamic features, and deep features. The proposed method is validated on industrial aluminum electrolysis data with an accuracy of 93.2°/0, which is better than the existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Cycle: Visible to Infrared Ship Image Translation Based on CycleGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Detecting targets in infrared ship images is crucial for various applications, such as maritime rescue and ship inspection. Training contemporary mainstream detection and segmentation models, however, requires large-scale, high-quality infrared ship image datasets. In open-world maritime confrontation scenarios, the complex and variable environment, scarcity of target ships, and limited acquisition conditions make it challenging to construct high-quality infrared ship image datasets. To address this issue, this paper proposes an unpaired visible-infrared ship image translation model based on CycleGAN, named Fuzzy-Cycle. The model introduces a fuzzy cycle loss to encourage the model to learn feature mapping rules between different domains while minimizing attention to unnecessary features. Additionally, the method employs U-Net as the generator network to retain shallow image features during upsampling and selects PatchGAN as the discriminator network, embedding Haar wavelet transform to enhance the discriminator's ability to analyze image frequency domain features. Experiments on the VAIS dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms mainstream unpaired image transfer models, showing excellent performance in the task of visible-infrared ship image translation. Furthermore, zero-shot image translation experiments on the HRSC2016 dataset prove the generalizability and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Energy-Saving Control of Air Conditioning Water System Based on Improved NSGA-II Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The energy consumed by the HVAC system to maintain thermal comfort inside the building accounts for more than 50% of its energy consumption. The water system is the core of the HVAC system, and unreasonable control of the water system will lead to a significant amount of energy consumption. Therefore, research on energy-saving control of the water system is very important. Currently there are many optimization methods used for energy-saving control of air-conditioning water systems, but there is still a lack of research on optimization methods that ensure both indoor comfort and energy-saving effects, and most studies only focus on the control of one side of the water system. In response to the above problems, an improved non-dominant sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) method is proposed to optimize the operating parameters on both sides of chilling and cooling, so as to control both sides of the water system. The method is guided by the predicted load value, experimented on the simstore simulation platform, and compared with the fixed water supply temperature control of the air-conditioning water system and the unimproved NSGA-II algorithm control. The results show that the control strategy proposed in this paper has achieved an average energy-saving rate of 11.58% in the air-conditioning water system, and the thermal comfort has increased by 2.24%.

articleTitle: HSV Color Space Based Automated Chemical Titrator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of long manual titration time, cumbersome operation, reliance on human eye judgment, and errors in titration endpoint in chemical quantitative testing. This paper designs a automatic chemical solution titration equipment and proposes a titration recognition method based on HSV color space. A typical chemical titration color model is established, and the RGB color space is transformed into HSV color space for titration area recognition and titration endpoint recognition. At the same time, an electrical control system with a microcontroller as the core, including a Micro infusion Syringe Pump, a mobile screw, a stirring device, and a visual light source, as well as an upper computer monitoring software for recognition algorithm implementation and human-machine interaction, is designed. Taking the determination of soil organic matter content as an example, the performance test was carried out, and the test results show that the titration error of the device is less than 0.3 ml, and it is more efficient than the manual titration, with good recognition rate and control accuracy. It not only solves the problem of human resources and the intervention of the human factor, but also overcomes the defects of inaccurate discrimination that occurs in the traditional use of the RGB color space as the basis for judging the end point of the titration.

articleTitle: A New Robust Learning Algorithm for Ordinary Differential Equation Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The data modeling of complex systems typically exhibits characteristics such as strong nonlinearity, variable redundancy, and abnormal data, all of which tend to decrease the model performance. To solve these problems, a robust learning algorithm for an ordinary differential equation (ODE) network is proposed. Firstly, the ODE network is trained as the basic model. Secondly, a novel loss function combines a Huber loss with elastic net regularization technique is designed. The proposed loss function has excellent resistance to outliers in the data and can make the model genialize better. Thirdly, a nonnegative garrote algorithm is introduced to reduce the redundancy of input variables and the model complexity. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified on a time series Friedman dataset and an industrial process dataset, compared with other data-driven modeling algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively select relevant input variables, simplify the model structure, and improve the generalization performance of the model.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Vehicular Systems and Platoons
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper studies adaptive control of vehicular systems and platoons, focusing on electric vehicles. An adaptive control law, closely related to the MIT-rule, is employed to control the vehicular longitudinal motion. Its use in cooperative adaptive cruise control is analyzed. Different from the known work in the existing literature, model nonlinearities and parameter uncertainties are taken into consideration. It is reported that the proposed adaptive control law renders the uncertain nonlinear vehicular system strict output passive and the closed-loop vehicular system admitting the £<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-gain strictly smaller than 1 without estimating vehicular parameters. Furthermore, the distributed adaptive control law achieves the string stability related to velocity synchronization and inter-vehicle distances. Simulation results are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control law.

articleTitle: A Novel Detection Scheme for Generalized Spatial Modulation System Based on Sparse Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high complexity of traditional detection algorithms for generalized spatial modulation system.the theory of compressed sensing was used to construct a signal detection model. According to the sparse property of generalized spatial modulation signals, a stagewise orthogonal matching pursuit detection algorithm based on sparse reconstruction was proposed. The active antenna index sequence was selected according to the correlation threshold judgment and the foreseen sparsity was not needed in the iterative process of the algorithm, the index set and signal residuals were updated.then the sent data was restored based on optimized termination condition and signal quantization. Analysis and experiments show the algorithm has smaller root mean square error and the detection performance is improved compared with reconstruction algorithms of the same category,and has substantially lower complexity compared with the maximum likelihood algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fractional Order PID Control for Green Hydrogen Ammonia Synthesis Tower Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Renewable energy offers the benefits of ecological harmony and enduring progress. However, due to its inherent volatility, the temperature in the ammonia synthesis tower fluctuates during the green hydrogen synthesis ammonia process. To address the issue, a temperature control method for the ammonia synthesis tower based on Fractional Order PIλDμ (FOPID) is proposed. Firstly, the ammonia synthesis tower model is established, and a cascaded control strategy for the hot spot temperature system is determined. Secondly, an Optuna optimization algorithm, employing an adaptive evolutionary strategy sampler based on the covariance matrix, is introduced to optimize the parameters of the FOPID controller. Comparative simulations of the temperature control system in the ammonia synthesis tower reveal the enhanced performance of the PIλDμ controller optimized through Optuna, surpassing traditional PID methodologies. Under PIλDμ controller, the system overshoot is reduced by 2.6%, the settling time is reduced by 5.9%, and the system's setpoint tracking capability, disturbance rejection ability, and robustness are improved.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-Layer Dynamic Multivariate Prediction Model for Power System Time Series Data Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting is an important but challenging problem in future power system. Existing fore-casting models struggle to handle the increasing amount of time series data due to the continuous upgrading of system structures, leading to a decrease in model performance and making it difficult to meet the accurate prediction and response speed requirements of the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multilayer dynamic multi-type prediction model based on deep learning, designed to adapt to the complex and diverse dynamic changes brought about by the high uncertainty of renewable energy sources in future power systems. Firstly, the model introduces a dynamic variable convolutional structure to address the different application scenarios of multiple regions and roles in real power systems. Secondly, a three-task prediction framework is proposed to adapt to the multi-scale features of temporal information in power systems. Then, an imbalanced prediction structure is designed to concentrate computing re-sources on the main tasks. Finally, to meet the fast response requirements of the prediction system, a combination of linear and nonlinear structures is proposed to construct a dynamic multivariate forecasting model, simplifying the network structure design and accelerating training speed while ensuring prediction performance. Experiments on three real datasets demonstrate the strong generalization performancestrong generalization performance and effectiveness of this model in complex multivariate time series forecasting.

articleTitle: Task Allocation and Path Planning for Multiple Destinations Oriented Towards Task Updates
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This study addresses the complexities of orchestrating multi-target transportation tasks within multi-agent systems, constrained by load capacity. The primary objective is to engineer an advanced path planning framework that assures collision avoidance and optimal load distribution. Diverging from conventional single-path strategies, this research incorporates load factors and requires continuous dynamic multi-target point and path planning to ensure agents can efficiently navigate through a series of predetermined key points. To address this complex requirement, a two-stage multi-agent task allocation and path planning method is proposed. First, an initial solution is obtained using a suboptimal algorithm, followed by optimization iterations using the large neighborhood search algorithm to improve task allocation. In the second stage, an accelerated algorithm based on priority search is used to plan optimal paths for each agent in a predetermined order. The proposed algorithm's effectiveness is comprehensively evaluated through a series of experimental evaluations and comparisons with the commercial solver Gurobi within a limited time. The results show that the proposed method achieves optimality in both running time and minimum path cost while ensuring the load balance of agents.

articleTitle: Temperature Feedforward Model Based on Improved Stochastic Configuration Network for Coal Mill
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Aiming at the practical needs for feedforward mod-eling of the coal mill outlet temperature setpoint under blended coal operation conditions, an improved stochastic configuration network (ISCN) is introduced for predictive modeling. Firstly, the stochastic configuration of hidden node parameters based on the supervision mechanism leads to uncertainty and cannot guarantee parameter optimality. Consequently, an improved pelican optimization algorithm (IPOA) is introduced to optimize the configuration of hidden node parameters, which not only enhances network learning efficiency but also lightweights the network structure. On the other hand, fully supervised SCN mod-eling demands large amount of high-cost experimental data. To reduce modeling expenses, a semi-supervised learning approach based on small labeled data is employed to categorize unlabeled data and expand the training dataset. Nextly, considering that there are some irrationalities in determining the coal mill outlet temperature setpoint using traditional methods. The ISCN introced in this paper is applied to feedforward model of coal mill outlet temperature setpoint. Finally, the validity and practicality of the method are verified by experiments.

articleTitle: MPC-Based Path Tracking Control for Autonomous Vehicles on Varying Friction Roads
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The focus on autonomous vehicles (AVs) has been steadily increasing lately, owing to the development of new technologies. While path tracking control is a significant module of autonomous driving, some control methods fail to consider friction variations on actual roads. By integrated consideration of road friction variations on the tracking performance, this paper proposes a new model predictive control (MPC) method taking into account desired curvature and designed adaptive speed. Moreover, an adaptive weight strategy is proposed in this new MPC framework based on variations in road friction and vehicle speed. Co-simulations considering varying road friction conditions were conducted for autonomous vehicles by CarSim and MATLAB/Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. Findings indicate that the suggested MPC can effectively achieve safe and comfortable path tracking under different friction coefficient road conditions, both at low and high initial speeds.

articleTitle: Characterisation of complex system Dynamics from data: A probing excitation method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: For complex dynamic systems, due to their intrinsic nonlinearity, time-varying and multivariate interdependence, they usually contain multiple inputs and multiple outputs, and the complex interactions and dynamics within the time and space of the system are also complex for the study of complex system physical properties. Therefore, in order to study complex dynamic systems, obtain their physical properties, and describe and predict the system behavior, this paper adopts a novel data-driven approach with the probing excitation method. The probing excitation method proposed in this paper distinguishes itself from traditional machine learning methods. Complex dynamic systems are usually black-box systems or partially black-box systems, while traditional methods for black-box systems construct black-box models that lack physical interpretability. The method in this paper enables the detection of physical properties of complex dynamical systems by selecting inputs and outputs and constructing models that reflect the physical properties. The probing excitation method involves selecting one input and one output of a complex dynamic system to build a model with interpretability that reflects the physical properties or some of the physical properties of this system. Repeat this process to develop multiple models and integrate them for comprehensive analysis. In this way, we can capture the system's physical characteristics, enhancing interpretability and enabling the prediction and control of system behavior.

Author Keywords: Multi degree of freedom linear system

articleTitle: Deployment of Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation Algorithm Based on NMPC Onto Unitree Go2Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the development of versatile control algorithms for quadruped robots, with a specific focus on the Unitree Go2. Traditional control algorithms often lack generalizability and require custom adaptations based on the robot's hardware or specific movement tasks. In response, we present a control algorithm for the Unitree Go2, which integrates a joint-free centroid dynamics model and a comprehensive body dynamics model. By prioritizing variables such as the linear and angular acceleration of the centroid and the swing leg trajectory, we utilize an open-source switching system optimal control toolbox to construct and solve a nonlinear model predictive controller. This controller effectively plans the movement trajectories for the robot's centroid and limbs, translating these into control signals for the joints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control scheme not only enables smooth movement on flat terrain but also enhances stability and robustness on uneven surfaces, preventing falls.

articleTitle: Dominant Feature Selection Methods for Root Cause Identification in Injection Moulding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid feature selection and classification validation approach for anomaly detection to identify major failure root causes using supervised classification validation. The proposed method is tested on real industry datasets from the manufacturing injection moulding process. Results indicate that the SMOTE technique effectively generates a balanced dataset for the minority class in both testing and training subsets, thereby improving model accuracy without altering the raw data samples. Pearson's correlation emerged as the best feature selection method when compared to Decision Tree and Recursive Feature Elimination methods. Random Forest was identified as the optimal classification model for anomaly detection using the case study datasets. This hybrid feature selection approach demonstrates that the study results can be applied to identify major root causes, thereby improving the quality performance of the injection moulding process.

articleTitle: A Motion Intent Recognition Method Based on Dynamic Feature Fusion and Multi-Stream TCN
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Clinical motor relearning theory emphasizes the active participation of patients, so the recognition of patient's motor imagery plays a key role in robot-assisted rehabilitation exercise training. We constructed an upper limb rehabilitation sEMG (Surface Electromyography) dataset by capturing 18 upper limb rehabilitation movements using a wireless sEMG acquisition system and proposed a deep learning model based on dynamic feature fusion with a multi-stream Temporal Convolutional Network (MS-TCN), which identified the patient's motor intention from the captured sEMG by end-to-end learning. On the one hand, the method can extract the temporal features of single-channel signals through the multi-stream TCN structure, and on the other hand, dynamic feature fusion can effectively utilize the primary-secondary relationship of multiple muscles in completing different motions, achieving high recognition accuracy and low response time. Through simulation analysis and experimental testing, the results show that this method can achieve higher classification accuracy than mainstream motor intention recognition algorithms on different subjects, and the effective use of this method will promote the recovery of patient's limb function and significantly improve the efficiency of rehabilitation training.

Author Keywords: Intelligent biomimetic upper limb rehabilitation system

articleTitle: Penetration-Free Collision Detection and Response Algorithm Based on Extended Position-Based Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In the virtual simulation platform, frequent physical interactions between the robot and the environment poses extremely high demands on the handling of collisions and contacts in the simulation. Current mainstream virtual simulation platforms, in pursuit of real-time performance, have sacrificed some accuracy in simulation algorithms, leading to control strategies obtained in training that are difficult to directly transfer to actual physical machines. This virtual-physical discrepancy has significantly impacted the efficiency and effectiveness of mobile robot simulation. Existing work has attempted to use more accurate mathematical modeling and design more realistic solvers, but at the cost of uncontrollable problem scale and extremely high computational complexity. Starting from this perspective, this paper designs a non-penetration simulation algorithm based on extended Position-Based Dynamics (XPBD), which improves the physical processing accuracy during the simulation while ensuring real-time performance, enhances the fidelity of the simulation, and reduces the virtual-physical discrepancy. Simulation experiments have been conducted to validate the reliability of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics of Industrial Quality KPIs Using Scalable Gaussian Mixture Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The Variational Inference Gaussian Mixture Model (VI-GMM) has been widely employed in multimode process modeling due to its inherent ability to automatically ascertain the optimal number of mixture components. Despite its advantages, the VI-GMM faces a significant computational challenge when dealing with large datasets, as it processes all data samples in each parameter update iteration. To address this issue, this paper introduces a novel approach: the Stochastic Variational Inference Gaussian Mixture Model (SVI-GMM). By leveraging the SVI algorithm to maximize the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), the scalability of the traditional VI-GMM is significantly enhanced, making it suitable for handling large- scale datasets. Furthermore, this study extends the application of SVI-GMM to its regression variant, SVI-GMR, for the forecasting of quality-related Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). The efficacy of the proposed methodology is demonstrated through a numerical example and a case study involving real-world industrial quality prediction modeling with extensive process data. These examples underscore the effectiveness and robustness of the SVI-GMM and SVI-GMR algorithms in providing accurate and scalable solutions for quality-related KPI predictions in big data environments.

articleTitle: A Insulator Defect Detection Method Based on YOLO and ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Insulators are crucial components in power system transmission and distribution, operating in complex environments. Prolonged exposure to open-air conditions can lead to various faults, impacting the reliability of power supply and the overall safety and stability of the power system. This paper presents an insulator inspection system based on YOLOv8 and ChatGPT, which enhances the efficiency and accuracy of insulator defect detection. The system can automatically generate reports using ChatGPT, integrating traditional inspection methods with ChatGPT, thus aiding engineers in understanding and addressing faults. This paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 model that incorporates the LSKA attention mechanism and DCNv4 deformable convolution. An insulator detection system integrating ChatGPT and the enhanced YOLOv8 model is developed. Experimental results show that the improved model increases accuracy by 1.6% for dirty glass sheets, 2.2% for dirty polymer sheets, 5.6% for defective polymer sheets, and 3.1% for insulator flashover. The overall mAP50 improved by 1.2%. These results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8 algorithm can accurately detect insulators, confirming the reasonableness and effectiveness of the enhancements.

articleTitle: Networked Control System: Development and Prospect
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The feedback control system, which is closed loop through the real time network, is called the networked control system. Because of the existence of the control loop network, the analysis and design of the networked control system become complex. The traditional control theory should be re-evaluated before it can be applied to the networked control system. A large number of literatures and research works have focused on the analysis and design of networked control system from different perspectives. The purpose of this paper is to introduce the current research status of networked control system, discuss and point out the future development issues and problems to be solved.

articleTitle: Research on Joint Optimization of Single Train's Delay Reduction and Energy-Saving Operation Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing urban rail transit operations during emergencies, aiming to reduce train traction energy consumption and expedite delay recovery by jointly optimizing arrival/departure times at each station and the operational trajectory between stations. A 3D STS (Space-Time-Speed) network is created to merge macroscopic train timetable scheduling with microscopic train operation trajectory optimization. By appropriately setting dimension resolutions, the system approximates the train's position, speed, and acceleration, transforming the complex train operation problem into a more manageable path planning challenge. Propose dual objectives: minimize net traction energy and delay time, aiming to reduce overall train operating costs and delays. Weighted summation combines objectives into a single nonlinear optimization. Dynamic programming then tackles the transformed path planning problem. The simulation results of Beijing Yizhuang Line show that while delay increases energy consumption, judicious selection of train operation trajectory can significantly reduce the energy consumption of the train. Factoring in energy consumption yields a 15.43% reduction compared to disregarding it, ensuring more efficient energy use without disrupting normal train operations.

articleTitle: PIGWN: Physics-Informed Graph WaveNet for Airport Flight Traffic Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The continuous growth of global travel demand leads to the continuous rise of airport flight flow, leading a rising need to accurately predict the airport flight traffic flow. Current research predominantly employs Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCN) to model intra-airport traffic changes, but overlooks comprehensive modeling of air traffic routes and temporal dimensions. Furthermore, existing models rely on data-driven approaches lacking a deep understanding of traffic change mechanisms, resulting in poor performance in new scenarios. To solve these problems, we propose a deep learning network framework Physics-Informed Graph WaveNet (PIGWN) based on multi-scale feature data fusion and constructs two new airport domain data sets. We integrated a physics-based module prior to GraphWaveNet to learn and integrate multi-scale spatio-temporal information of airports, embedding physical formulas reflecting airport traffic changes. The physics learning module fuses multi-scale spatio-temporal feature data considering the time delay and traffic conservation relationship between different airports. The Graph WaveNet (GWN) structure learns and predicts multi-scale spatio-temporal feature data, and uses the time-space convolution block model to capture and model spatio-temporal features. PIGWN model has certain theoretical significance and practical application value in the field of airport flight flow prediction, which realizes the accurate prediction of airport flight flow and provides certain decision support and reference for air traffic management. We have made the code publicly available at https://github.com/yzc0912/PIGWN.

articleTitle: Hybrid Classification Method for Anomaly Detection in Injection Moulding Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Industrial and environmental challenges faced in injection moulding processes push manufacturing companies to embrace smart manufacturing and adopt machine learning to deal with anomaly detection. Challenges arisen from imbalanced dataset gives rise to the development of our novel hybrid classification method. A novel hybrid classification method for anomaly detection in injection moulding is proposed in this paper. The proposed method involves feature selection with K-Means Clustering to remove noise data prior to Multi-Layer Perceptron. Feature selection helps to reduce the high-dimension of the dataset. K-Means Clustering helps to remove noise data that will have similar patterns with data of another class label. Multi-Layer Perceptron is used to verify the training accuracy and to build train model. Real industrial dataset of injection moulding process from a local manufacturing company is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in this paper. The proposed hybrid method outperforms other classical models such as Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Decision Tree (DT) and CNN (Convolutional Neural Network). It successfully increases the failure detect rate and reduces false reject rate up to 90%.

articleTitle: A Review of Similarity-Based Few-Shot Learning Methods for Time Series Classification in Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: The classification of time series data is crucial in nu-merous fields, including manufacturing, where high-dimensional and complex temporal data are prevalent. Traditional methods often require extensive labeled datasets, posing challenges in cost and time. Few-shot learning (FSL) offers a solution by enabling models to generalize from a minimal number of labeled examples. This paper reviews the current state-of-the-art in FSL techniques for time series classification, emphasizing manufacturing applications. It covers various deep learning architectures such as Siamese Networks, Prototypical Networks, Matching Networks, Memory-Augmented Neural Networks, and Transformers. The survey highlights the strengths and limitations of these models in handling the unique challenges of manufacturing time series data, including high dimensionality, complex temporal depen-dencies, multisensor fusion, noise, and missing data. Through comprehensive analysis, this paper aims to provide insights into the potential of FSL in enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of time series classification in manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Distributed Finite-Time Consensus Control of Multi-Agent Systems with Communication Topology Switching*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In this paper, in the context of distributed control of heterogeneous battery energy storage systems in a droop control microgrid, based on the consensus theory of multi-agent systems, this paper proposes a distributed finite-time control strategy. Each agent in this strategy only needs to obtain its own information and neighbor information through a sparse communication network, and the topology of the communication network between the agents is time-varying, and its switching process satisfies the Markov process, which enables the multi-intelligent agent system to reach an average consensus in finite time under the condition of the limitation of the number of controllers. The theoretical analysis clearly reveals the consistency and convergence of the proposed control strategy. In addition, the proposed control strategy improves the synchronization performance over the traditional one. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy is also verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Batch Process Monitoring with Attention-Based Two-Dimensional Stacked Graph Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In batch processes, the efficacy of statistical control is reportedly sensitive to the dynamics and nonlinearity found in the batch data, which can hamper the valid feature extraction for statistical analysis. Normally, a two-way window is applied to aggregate the samples across the batch and time direction to assuage this challenge. However, samples in the window are generally processed on par with each other such that irrelevant features can cause redundancy and make window size critical to be tediously tune during the training phase. In this paper, a linear correlation aided method is proposed to first determine the effective size of a regular-shaped sliding window, and, a Euclidean distance-based measure is used to construct a graph prior to the phase of feature extraction. With these efforts, we presented the Attention-based Two-dimensional Stacked Graph Convolutional Autoencoder (2D-ASGCA) for enhanced learning in the Statistical Process Control (SPC) of batch processes. Moreover, a technique called Deep Reconstruction-based Contribution (DRBC) chart has been applied to perform the variable-wise root cause diagnosis, when a fault is signaled. Finally, two case studies are provided to demonstrate the model validity.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control Based on Fuzzy-MPC for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: In recent years, autonomous vehicles (AVs) have gained significant interests and it is expected that fully- autonomous vehicles will be appearing on roads soon. Trajectory tracking plays a crucial role in the driving tasks of autonomous vehicles. While classic model predictive control (MPC) is a common tracking method, it may not work well when encoun-tering sharp bends or curves. Aiming at solving this issue, this paper integrates fuzzy rules with classic MPC to design a new control method, namely, F-MPC. Fuzzy rules are set by considering curve radius, expected speed and steering angle of the reference trajectory. Then, the expected steering angle in the MPC model is adjusted according to the set fuzzy rules to achieve better tracking performance. In addition, the constraints are reasonably adaptive to the steering system of the actual vehicle. The effectiveness and advantages of the proposed trajectory tracking method have been verified through simulations and experiments on the CarSim-MATLAB/Simulink environment and QCar experimental platform in tracking S-shape trajectory.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Pre-Training Improves Anomaly Detection in Fused Magnesium Smelting Process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection is essential for the fused magnesium smelting process. Existing researches typically pursuing network structure to improve model performance, while overlooking the influence of data scale for training. To tackle the problem of limited labeled data in real industrial scenarios, this paper utilizes network pre-trained on large-scale public dataset, ImageNet1K, alleviating the issue of insufficient samples for fused magnesium furnace anomaly detection. This paper also uses a large-scale fused magnesium furnace anomaly dataset FMF-Big for a baseline comparison. The empirically study shows that, even though the data in ImageNet1K differs greatly from the fused magnesium furnace scenario, the pre-trained model brought a 1.81% increase in accuracy (97.59% detection accuracy). To our best knowledge, this is the first exploration to investigate the impact of large-scale pre-training on the anomaly detection in fused magnesium smelting process. We believe the study will have inspiring implications for subsequent researches.

articleTitle: AI-Orchestrated Data-Driven Modelling and Control in Battery Management Systems: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Industrial Artificial Intelligence (IAI)
abstract: Battery storage is playing an important role in supporting the low-carbon transition of the energy systems from the top to the tail. For example, Lithium-ion batteries have been widely used in electric vehicles and renewable energy storage systems. However, the efficient management and control of these batteries pose a multitude of challenges. Inappropriate battery operating activities could significantly damage the health of the battery systems, and even cause safety concerns. Constructing suitable battery models to predict the battery states and developing reliable control strategies to avoid unsafe operations are significantly important. The recent development of artificial intelligence technology provides novel tools for battery operation and control due to its ability to handle large datasets. This paper presents a brief review of the latest progress in AI-orchestrated methods in battery modelling and control. The paper in particular focuses on the latest progress in machine learning and deep neural networks for the battery management system.
